Count code points and conversion lengths

Source: R/count.R
utf_count.Rd

utf_count() counts the code points (characters, in the sense of nchar(type = "chars")) of each element. utf_length_as() gives the number of bytes converting each element from from to to will produce, without converting it.

Usage

utf_count(x, encoding = "UTF-8", useBytes = FALSE)

utf_length_as(x, from = "UTF-8", to)

Arguments

x

A character vector, a raw vector (one element), or a list of raw vectors (one element each). NA strings and NULL list elements give NA.

encoding, from

The encoding of the input: "UTF-8", "UTF-16LE", "UTF-16BE", "UTF-16", "UTF-32LE", "UTF-32BE", "UTF-32" or "Latin-1", matched without regard to case or hyphens; utf_count() also takes "ASCII". A character vector is UTF-8 text, so for one only "UTF-8" applies, unless useBytes = TRUE in utf_count().

useBytes

For a character vector: FALSE (the default) takes each string in its marked encoding and checks its UTF-8 form, refusing strings marked "bytes"; TRUE checks the bytes of every string as they are, which is how to check a string R believes is UTF-8.

to

The target encoding: "UTF-8", "UTF-16LE", "UTF-16BE", "UTF-32LE", "UTF-32BE" or "Latin-1".

Value

An integer vector, one value per element, NA where the element is NA, NULL or ill-formed. Counts beyond the integer range come back as doubles. A character vector or a list keeps its names.

Details

A leading byte-order mark that matches the input encoding is skipped and not counted, and a conversion writes none, so neither counts it. An element that is ill-formed in its encoding gives NA; utf_error_at() says where. With a "Latin-1" target every code point is one byte, those above U+00FF included, since a conversion writes one byte for each of them too (an error, ? or NA, as its invalid argument says).

See also

utf_valid(); nchar().

Examples

utf_count(c("abc", "caf\u00e9", "\U0001f600", NA))
#> [1]  3  4  1 NA
utf_count(as.raw(c(0x3d, 0xd8, 0x00, 0xde)), "UTF-16LE")   # one emoji
#> [1] 1

utf_length_as("caf\u00e9", to = "UTF-16LE")   # 8 bytes
#> [1] 8
utf_length_as("\U0001f600", to = "UTF-16LE")  # a surrogate pair: 4 bytes
#> [1] 4
utf_length_as(as.raw(c(0x63, 0xe9)), from = "Latin-1", to = "UTF-8")
#> [1] 3
